{key}: {value}\")\n50:         if self.current_task:\n51:             lines.append(f\"- Current task: {self.current_task}\")\n52:         return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n53: \n54: \n55: def dedup_repeated_blocks(text: str) -> str:\n56:     \"\"\"Remove exact duplicate paragraph blocks, keeping first occurrence order.\n57: \n58:     Operates on blank-line-separated blocks so repeated analyst reports in a\n59:     long history collapse to one copy instead of being sent N times.\n60:     \"\"\"\n61:     if not text:\n62:         return text\n63:     blocks = list(text.split(\"\\n\\n\"))\n64:     seen: set[str] = set()\n65:     kept: list[str] = []\n66:     for block in blocks:\n67:         key = block.strip()\n68:         if not key:\n69:             continue\n70:         if key in seen:\n71:             continue\n72:         seen.add(key)\n73:         kept.append(block)\n74:     return \"\\n\\n\".join(kept)\n75: \n76: \n77: def bound_history(text: str, max_chars: int = 6000) -> str:\n78:     \"\"\"Bound total assembled history length by truncating from the tail.\"\"\"\n79:     if not text:\n80:         return text\n81:     if len(text) <= max_chars:\n82:         return text\n83:     # Cut at a block boundary near the limit so we never split mid-paragraph.\n84:     cut = text.rfind(\"\\n\\n\", 0, max_chars)\n85:     if cut == -1:\n86:         cut = max_chars\n87:     return text[:cut].rstrip() + \"\\n\\n[... earlier history truncated ...]\"\n88: \n89: \n90: def estimate_token_heuristic(text: str) -> int:\n91:     \"\"\"Deterministic English-token heuristic for offline comparisons.\n92: \n93:     This is a *character-based heuristic*, explicitly NOT claimed as provider\n94:     token counts; real token numbers come from LLM usage metadata. Extend through `src/research_desk/`; application tests belong in `test/offline/` and API-dependent experiments in `test/live/`. Reuse the real TradingAgentsGraph and its selected market/news, research, trader, risk and portfolio roles. No replacement graph, fabricated market data labeled real, or broker access.\n\nApplication module ownership is defined in the blueprint. Policy constants belong to `research_desk.config`; business policy belongs to `research_desk.policy`; approval and state transitions belong to `research_desk.review`; transactions belong to `research_desk.storage`. Avoid shared vendor branches specific to Research Desk. An interface must be located before use. New interfaces require updated callers and contract tests.\n\n## Authority and change control\n\nModel output is advisory. It cannot approve a proposal, choose policy constants, set an evidence price, or mutate the ledger. Approval binds exact terms. Hold, REVIEW and incomplete research do not trade. Valid sells never exceed owned shares. Every execution rechecks current holdings and cash.\n\nThe plan/test decision in `docs/process/test-approval.yaml` predates this implementation and authorizes its three-feature scope. It does not authorize unrelated future changes. Changes to policy, approval, permission files or persistent contracts need an ADR and a leo decision covering the concrete change. `.opencode/rules.md`, `.agent/rules.md`, test approvals and permission decisions are owned by leo; implementation agents may propose changes but must not overwrite them.\n\nOpenCode generates and modifies application, tests and CI. The coordinating workflow supplies prompts, runs commands and maintains evidence/report documents. Credentials are supplied only as host environment variables at runtime; never read global credential files or serialize secrets. Use the isolated project `.venv` and explicit DeepSeek model. Do not change the parent workspace's `.venv`.\n\n## Verification and completion\n\nUse the approved AT-01 through AT-08 specifications. At least one meaningful negative test per feature is required. Before a final change, run all `tests/` and `test/offline/` tests. Static checks and requirements schema must pass. Fixed semantic replay is part of the prompt/model change gate; live evaluations require saved actual usage and scores. The concrete plan and tests were approved at 12:05:17.791955 UTC before OpenCode's first implementation event at 12:06:32.695 UTC.\n4: \n5: ## Context and alternatives\n6: \n7: TradingAgents v0.4.0 already provides multi-agent research, structured decisions, date-aware memory, checkpointing and price validation. The missing product workflow is portable evidence followed by explicit approval and paper execution. A complete graph rewrite would discard tested domain behavior and make the optimization baseline incomparable. Editing every upstream prompt and tool would distribute application-specific policy across many owners. A narrow application extension keeps the experimental boundary visible.\n8: \n9: Candidate A modifies the entire graph and shared vendors. Candidate B subclasses/composes the existing graph and implements policy outside it. Candidate C builds a small new agent demo. The evaluation table selects B because it preserves genuine AI integration while keeping deterministic authority isolated. The original graph's full selected role sequence is retained in both experimental arms.\n10: \n11: ## Context layers and assembly\n12: \n13: Layer1 identifies the instrument and analysis cutoff. Layer2 states standing constraints: use available evidence, retain source identity, distinguish unknown facts and keep execution advisory. Layer3 supplies frozen market/history/news knowledge. Layer4 holds current discussion and retrieved past context. Layer5 preserves resumable structured state. Layer6 gives the current agent task and expected output.\n14: \n15: The assembly order is eligibility filtering, duplicate removal in compact mode, prioritization, budget accounting, compaction and final constraint reinjection. Baseline preserves original substantive prompt input. Compact can remove repeated paragraphs or shorten older discussion, while retaining symbol, date, price evidence, source IDs and current task. It also requests concise role output to reduce repeated prose passed to later agents. Fresh six-case runs have little past memory, so compact must apply to actual per-agent messages; changing only a memory string would leave the dominant token cost unchanged.\n16: \n17: The call budget is configured for the experiment. Per-call maximum output bounds use the provider's existing max_tokens contract. Character estimates may guide context assembly but never replace provider-reported token usage. The model adapter checks before starting a request; a structured-output retry cannot create an extra request after the budget is exhausted. Critical constraints are re-injected after compaction. Factual quality is evaluated independently of brevity.\n18: \n19: ## Consequences and reopening conditions\n20: \n21: Evidence packs contain prompts and responses and are larger than ordinary reports. Replay is fast because it reconstructs captured state; controlled reruns call the model and remain stochastic. The frozen provider must answer valid parameter variations from data, because an exact tool-transcript lookup would bias the comparison when compact changes tool arguments.\n22: \n23: The approval boundary stays outside all model tools. The extension retains responsibility for current-ledger checks even if upstream research changes. Reopen this ADR if an upstream public interface cannot expose a material external read, if multiuser concurrency is added, or if compact cannot satisfy factual constraints without discarding agent roles. The frozen provider must answer valid parameter variations from data, because an exact tool-transcript lookup would bias the comparison when compact changes tool arguments.\n\nThe approval boundary stays outside all model tools. The extension retains responsibility for current-ledger checks even if upstream research changes. +# Focused review corrections for the CI gates
+
+Complete only these real gate issues. No app source/test/fixture edits, no installs, no whole-suite loop. Preserve your six gate design and public CLI. Read the current files before editing because the parallel document/source owner may have supplied AT-07 by now.
+
+1. `_gate_lib.changed_files` must fail the gate on git failure; returning an empty list currently makes an invalid diff pass. Local porcelain parsing uses `line.strip()` before removing the status columns, losing the first filename character for ` M file`. Prefer actual `git diff --name-only`, cached diff, and `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` to enumerate modified/staged/untracked individual files. Preserve real nonzero exits. For PR workflows compare the actual PR base SHA to head SHA, not a best-effort missing ref. Explicit changed-files remains useful for negative demonstrations.

+2. Gate 1 currently says a previous approval is automatically in force for any changed test, which does not enforce the requirement. Validate the evidence path exists as well as plan/test-plan/approval-record paths. Check declared versions against the versions in the actual referenced documents. In PR/base-ref mode, changes to test specifications or test files require `docs/process/test-approval.yaml` to be updated in that same change; a source-only fix may reuse unchanged already-approved tests. Validate the actual timezone-aware order and AT-01..08 coverage. Do not infer approval of arbitrary new tests from the existence of old AT identifiers. The initial delivery includes the approval and all its references in the same PR, while the actual recorded approval precedes implementation.

Read the changed ADRs and require coverage of the changed owner/path, and require the actual approval marker/owner present in the real decision documents. Do not invent a separate approval schema. Current files include `docs/process/test-approval.yaml` and ADRs owned by leo. Include persistent models and permission/config files in safety paths as declared by permission-model.md. from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def project_root() -> Path:
    """Repo root: this file lives in ``<root>/scripts/``."""
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def resolve_root(root: str | None) -> Path:
    return Path(root).resolve() if root else project_root()


def tool_path(root: Path, name: str) -> str:
    """Prefer the isolated project venv, then the PATH executable."""
    local = root / ".venv" / "bin" / name
    if local.exists():
        return str(local)
    found = shutil.which(name)
    if found:
        return found
    return str(local)


def run(cmd: list[str], cwd: Path | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    """Run a command, capturing output. Exit status is not masked here."""
    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)


def _parse_status_line(line: str) -> str | None:
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        return None
    # porcelain v1: "XY path" (renames/copies include a second path segment).
    if len(line) > 3:
        return line[3:].split(" -> ")[0].strip()
    return None


def changed_files(
    root: Path,
    base_ref: str | None = None,
    head_ref: str | None = None,
    explicit: str | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Resolve the set of changed file paths for a change gate.

    Priority: an explicit ``--changed-files`` list (enables reproducible
    negative examples without editing the repo), else a git base..head diff,
    else the working-tree changes (modified + untracked) so initial/local work
    is handled honestly rather than pretending nothing changed.
    """
    if explicit:
        return [f.strip() for f in explicit.split(",") if f.strip()]
    if base_ref:
        cmd = ["git", "-C", str(root), "diff", "--name-only", base_ref]
        if head_ref:
            cmd.append(head_ref)
        proc = run(cmd, root)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            print(f"ERROR: git diff failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}", file=sys.stderr)
            return []
        return [l for l in proc.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip()]
    proc = run(["git", "-C", str(root), "status", "--porcelain=v1"], root)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return []
    files = []
    for line in proc.stdout.splitlines():
        path = _parse_status_line(line)
        if path:
            files.append(path)
    return files


def add_change_args(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    parser.add_argument("--root", default=None, help="Repository root (defaults to project root).")
    parser.add_argument("--base-ref", default=None, help="Base ref for PR change detection.")
    parser.add_argument("--head-ref", default=None, help="Head ref for PR change detection.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--changed-files",

def wrap_llm_client_factory(
    orig_factory,
    context_mode: str,

    max_output_tokens: int = 1800,

    Used by the runner to scope compaction to the LLMs a single graph builds,
    without touching vendor or graph code. Baseline passes the client through

            return client

            def __init__(self, inner):
                self._inner = inner

            def get_llm(self):

                    self._inner.get_llm(),
                    context_mode,
                    max_output_tokens=max_output_tokens,
                    max_msg_chars=max_msg_chars,
                )

            def get_provider_name(self):
                return self._inner.get_provider_name()

            def warn_if_unknown_model(self):
                return self._inner.warn_if_unknown_model()

            def validate_model(self):

def _format_header(symbol: str, start_date: str, end_date: str, n: int) -> str:

        "# Data retrieved on: frozen corpus (no network)\n\n"
    )


class FrozenMarketProvider:
    """Read-only market provider backed by one immutable CSV."""

    def __init__(self, ticker: str, csv_path: str | Path | None = None):
        self.ticker = ticker.upper()
        self.csv_path = Path(csv_path) if csv_path else MARKET_DIR / f"{self.ticker}.csv"
        if not self.csv_path.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"frozen CSV not found: {self.csv_path}")
        self.frame = pd.read_csv(self.csv_path, parse_dates=["Date"])
        self.frame = self.frame.sort_values("Date").reset_index(drop=True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # stock data
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_stock_data(self, symbol: str, start_date: str, end_date: str) -> str:
        rows = self._rows_between(start_date, end_date)
        if rows.empty:
            return UNAVAILABLE
        out = self._to_upstream_csv(rows)
        header = _format_header(self.ticker, start_date, end_date, len(rows))
        return header + out

    def _rows_between(self, start_date: str, end_date: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        df = self.frame
        if start_date:
            df = df[df["Date"] >= pd.Timestamp(start_date)]
        if end_date:
            df = df[df["Date"] <= pd.Timestamp(end_date)]
        return df

    def _to_upstream_csv(self, rows: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
        out = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "Date": rows["Date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
                "Open": rows["Open"],
                "High": rows["High"],
                "Low": rows["Low"],
                "Close": rows["Close"],
                "Adj Close": rows["Adj Close"],
                "Volume": rows["Volume"],
            }
        )
        return out.to_csv(index=False)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # indicators
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_indicators(self, symbol: str, indicator: str, curr_date: str, look_back_days: int = 30) -> str:
        df = self._frame_as_of(curr_date, look_back_days)
        if df.empty or len(df) < 2:
            return UNAVAILABLE
        close = df["Close"]
        n = len(close)
        ind = (indicator or "").strip().lower()
        lines = [f"# Technical indicator for {self.ticker} as of {curr_date} (from frozen CSV)"]
        if ind in ("close_20_sma", "sma", "close_50_sma", "close_200_sma"):
            window = 20 if "20" in ind else (200 if "200" in ind else 50)
            w = min(window, n)
            val = close.iloc[-w:].mean()
            lines.append(f"{ind}: {val:.2f} (window {w} of {n} available rows)")
        elif ind in ("close_10_ema", "ema"):
            span = min(10, n)
            val = close.ewm(span=span, adjust=False).mean().iloc[-1]
            lines.append(f"{ind}: {val:.2f}")
        elif ind in ("rsi",):
            val = _rsi(close)
            lines.append(f"rsi: {val:.2f}")
        elif ind in ("boll", "boll_ub", "boll_lb"):
            mid = close.rolling(min(20, n)).mean().iloc[-1]
            std = close.rolling(min(20, n)).std().iloc[-1]
            lines.append(f"boll: {mid:.2f}")
            lines.append(f"boll_ub: {mid + 2 * std:.2f}")
            lines.append(f"boll_lb: {mid - 2 * std:.2f}")
        else:
            lines.append(f"{ind}: {close.iloc[-1]:.2f} (close)")
        lines.append(f"last_close: {close.iloc[-1]:.2f}")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def get_verified_market_snapshot(self, symbol: str, curr_date: str, look_back_days: int = 30) -> str:
        df = self._frame_as_of(curr_date, look_back_days)
        if df.empty:
            return UNAVAILABLE
        last = df.iloc[-1]
        return (
            f"# Verified market snapshot for {self.ticker} as of {curr_date}\n"
            f"last_close: {float(last['Close']):.2f}\n"
            f"last_open: {float(last['Open']):.2f}\n"
            f"day_high: {float(last['High']):.2f}\n"
            f"day_low: {float(last['Low']):.2f}\n"
            f"volume: {int(last['Volume'])}\n"
            f"as_of: {last['Date'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}\n"
        )

    def _frame_as_of(self, curr_date: str, look_back_days: int = 30) -> pd.DataFrame:
        df = self.frame
        if curr_date:
            df = df[df["Date"] <= pd.Timestamp(curr_date)]
        if look_back_days:
            df = df.tail(max(1, look_back_days))

        return UNAVAILABLE

def _rsi(close: pd.Series, period: int = 14) -> float:
    delta = close.diff()

```python
def changed_files(root, base_ref=None, head_ref=None, explicit=None):
    if explicit:
        return [f for f in explicit.split(",") if f.strip()]
    if base_ref:
        cmd = ["git", "-C", str(root), "diff", "--name-only"]
        cmd.append(base_ref)
        if head_ref:
            cmd.append(head_ref)
        proc = run(cmd, root)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"git diff failed (base={base_ref}, head={head_ref}): {proc.stderr.strip()}")
        files = [l for l in proc.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip()]
        if head_ref:
            # base..head already covers the range
            return files
        return files
    # no refs: working tree = modified + staged + untracked
    names = []
    for cmd in (
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "diff", "--name-only"],
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "diff", "--cached", "--name-only"],
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard"],
    ):
        proc = run(cmd, root)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"git status enumeration failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
        names.extend(l for l in proc.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip())
    # dedupe preserving order
    return list(dict.fromkeys(names))
```

```python
def _git(root: Path, args: list[str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return run(["git", "-C", str(root), *args], root)

def changed_files(root, base_ref=None, head_ref=None, explicit=None):
    if explicit:
        return [f.strip() for f in explicit.split(",") if f.strip()]
    if base_ref:
        cmd = ["diff", "--name-only", base_ref]
        if head_ref:
            cmd.append(head_ref)
        proc = _git(root, cmd)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"git diff failed (base={base_ref!r}, head={head_ref!r}): {proc.stderr.strip()}"
            )
        return [l for l in proc.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip()]
    names: list[str] = []
    for args in (
        ["diff", "--name-only"],
        ["diff", "--cached", "--name-only"],
        ["ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard"],
    ):
        proc = _git(root, args)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"git change enumeration failed ({args!r}): {proc.stderr.strip()}")
        names.extend(l for l in proc.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip())
    return list(dict.fromkeys(names))
```

+              "content": """"Shared helpers for the Research Desk CI gate scripts.

These scripts are CI glue and are intentionally small and free of live-service
dependencies. They only read the repository and run deterministic commands.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def project_root() -> Path:
    """Repo root: this file lives in ``<root>/scripts/``."""
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def resolve_root(root: str | None) -> Path:
    return Path(root).resolve() if root else project_root()


def tool_path(root: Path, name: str) -> str:
    """Prefer the isolated project venv, then the PATH executable."""
    local = root / ".venv" / "bin" / name
    if local.exists():
        return str(local)
    found = shutil.which(name)
    if found:
        return found
    return str(local)


def run(cmd: list[str], cwd: Path | None = None) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    """Run a command, capturing output. Exit status is not masked here."""
    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)


def _git(root: Path, args: list[str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return run(["git", "-C", str(root), *args], root)


def changed_files(
    root: Path,
    base_ref: str | None = None,
    head_ref: str | None = None,
    explicit: str | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Resolve the set of changed file paths for a change gate.

    Priority: an explicit ``--changed-files`` list (enables reproducible
    negative examples without editing the repo), else a git base..head diff,
    else the working-tree changes (modified + staged + untracked) so initial /
    local work is handled honestly rather than pretending nothing changed.

    A git failure raises ``RuntimeError`` so it becomes a gate failure; an
    invalid diff can never silently be treated as "no change".
    """
    if explicit:
        return [f.strip() for f in explicit.split(",") if f.strip()]
    if base_ref:
        cmd = ["diff", "--name-only", base_ref]
        if head_ref:
            cmd.append(head_ref)
        proc = _git(root, cmd)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"git diff failed (base={base_ref!r}, head={head_ref!r}): "
                f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}"
            )
        return [line for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    names: list[str] = []
    for args in (
        ["diff", "--name-only"],
        ["diff", "--cached", "--name-only"],
        ["ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard"],
    ):
        proc = _git(root, args)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"git change enumeration failed ({args!r}): "
                f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}"
            )
        names.extend(line for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip())
    return list(dict.fromkeys(names))


def add_change_args(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    parser.add_argument("--root", default=None, help="Repository root (defaults to project root).")
    parser.add_argument("--base-ref", default=None, help="Base ref for PR change detection.")
    parser.add_argument("--head-ref", default=None, help="Head ref for PR change detection.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--changed-files",
        default=None,
        help="Comma-separated explicit changed file list (negative-test override).",
    )


def fail(checks: list[str], failures: list[str]) -> None:
    """Print a consolidated gate result and exit nonzero if any check failed."""
    for line in checks:
        print(line)
    print("RESULT: FAIL" if failures else "RESULT: PASS")
    if failures:
        print("FAILURES:")
        for f in failures:
            print(f"- {f}")
        sys.exit(1)
    sys.exit(0)

def _parse_iso(value: str) -> datetime:
    dt = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
    if dt.tzinfo is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{value!r} is not timezone-aware")
    return dt


def _document_version(path: Path) -> str | None:
    """Extract the version declared on a referenced document (e.g. 版本：1.0.0)."""
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
    m = VERSION_RE.search(text)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def _resolve_changes(root: Path, args) -> list[str]:

        return changed_files(root, args.base_ref, args.head_ref, args.changed_files)
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        fail([], [f"could not resolve changed files: {exc}"])

    failures: list[str] = []

    if not approval_file.exists():
        fail(checks, [f"missing approval record: {approval_file}"])

    data = yaml.safe_load(approval_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    checks.append(f"read {approval_file}")

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        fail(checks, ["test-approval.yaml is not a YAML mapping"])

    for key in REQUIRED_KEYS:
        if key not in data:

    if data.get("decision") != "APPROVED":
        failures.append(f"decision must be APPROVED, got {data.get('decision')!r}")

    if data.get("approver") != APPROVER:

            f"got {data.get('approver')!r}"

    try:
        approved_at = _parse_iso(data["approved_at"])
        implemented_at = _parse_iso(data["implementation_started_at"])
        checks.append(f"approved_at={approved_at.isoformat()}")
        checks.append(f"implementation_started_at={implemented_at.isoformat()}")
        if not (approved_at < implemented_at):

    except KeyError:

    for name, ref in (

        ("test_plan", data.get("test_plan")),
        ("approval_record", data.get("approval_record")),

        if not p.exists():

    for name, ref, declared in (
        ("plan", data.get("plan"), data.get("plan_version")),
        ("test_plan", data.get("test_plan"), data.get("test_plan_version")),
    ):
        if not declared:

            continue
        doc = root / ref if isinstance(ref, str) and ref else None
        if doc is not None and doc.exists():
            doc_version = _document_version(doc)
            checks.append(f"{name}: declared {declared!r}, document {doc_version!r}")
            if doc_version is not None and doc_version != str(declared):

                    f"{name} version mismatch: approval declares {declared!r} "
                    f"but {ref} declares {doc_version!r}"
                )

    if not data.get("evidence"):
        failures.append("evidence reference is empty")
    if not data.get("scope"):
        failures.append("scope is empty")

    tests = data.get("tests") or []
    if not isinstance(tests, list):
        failures.append("tests must be a list")
        tests = []
    test_set = set(tests)
    checks.append(f"approved tests: {sorted(test_set)}")
    for tid in tests:
        if not isinstance(tid, str) or not tid.startswith("AT-") or len(tid) != 5:
            failures.append(f"malformed test id: {tid!r}")
    missing = REQUIRED_TESTS - test_set
    if missing:
        failures.append(f"approval does not cover all acceptance tests; missing: {sorted(missing)}")

    changed = _resolve_changes(root, args)
    if changed:
        test_change = [
            c for c in changed
            if c.startswith(TEST_FILE_PREFIXES) or c in TEST_SPEC_DOCS
        ]
        if test_change:
            checks.append(f"PR changes test specifications/files: {len(test_change)} file(s)")
            if APPROVAL_DOC not in changed:
                failures.append(
                    "test specification or test file changed without updating "
                    "docs/process/test-approval.yaml in the same change"
                )
            else:
                checks.append("test approval updated in the same change")
        else:
            checks.append(
                "no test specification/file change; existing approved tests may be reused "
                "for this source-only change"
            )

    fail(checks, failures)

# Modules that own deterministic authority and therefore must not touch an LLM.
NO_LLM_MODULES = ("policy", "review")

LLM_PROVIDER_PREFIXES = (
    "langchain",
    "openai",
    "anthropic",
    "google",

    "zhipu",
    "zhipuai",
    "minimax",

)

LLM_FACTORY_NAMES = {"create_llm_client", "create_llm"}
# Functions that grant approval or mutate the ledger; the graph must not import them.
LEDGER_AUTHORITY_NAMES = {
    "approve",
    "execute",
    "apply_transaction",

SAFETY_PATHS = (

def _import_names(tree: ast.Module) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    """Return (top-level module names, imported original member names).

    Uses the *original* imported names (``alias.name``) rather than only
    aliases, so ``from x import approve as y`` is still detected.
    """
    modules: list[str] = []
    members: list[str] = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            modules.extend(alias.name for alias in node.names)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            if node.module:
                modules.append(node.module)
            members.extend(alias.name for alias in node.names)
    return modules, members


def check_authority_boundary(root: Path, failures: list[str]) -> None:
    for mod in NO_LLM_MODULES:
        path = root / "src/research_desk" / f"{mod}.py"
        if not path.exists():
            failures.append(f"authority module missing: {path}")
            continue
        tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        modules, members = _import_names(tree)
        offending_modules = [
            m
            for m in modules
            if m.startswith(LLM_PROVIDER_PREFIXES) or m.startswith("tradingagents.llm_clients")
        ]
        offending_factories = [m for m in members if m in LLM_FACTORY_NAMES]
        if offending_modules or offending_factories:
            detail: list[str] = []
            if offending_modules:
                detail.append(f"LLM/provider imports: {sorted(set(offending_modules))}")
            if offending_factories:
                detail.append(f"LLM factory names: {sorted(set(offending_factories))}")
            failures.append(f"{mod}.py must not touch an LLM; {'; '.join(detail)}")

    graph_path = root / "src/research_desk/graph_adapter.py"
    if graph_path.exists():
        tree = ast.parse(graph_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        modules, members = _import_names(tree)
        forbidden = sorted(LEDGER_AUTHORITY_NAMES & set(members))
        if forbidden:
            failures.append(
                f"graph_adapter.py must not import approval/ledger-mutation "
                f"functions; found: {forbidden}"
            )
        if any(m == "research_desk.storage" or m.endswith(".storage") for m in modules):
            failures.append("graph_adapter.py must not import research_desk.storage")


def check_safety_path_evidence(
    root: Path, changed: list[str], failures: list[str]
) -> None:
    safety_changed = [c for c in changed if c in SAFETY_PATHS]
    if not safety_changed:
        return
    checks_ok = True
    changed_set = set(changed)
    adr_changed = sorted(
        p for p in changed if p.startswith(ADR_PREFIX) and p.endswith(".md")
    )
    approval_changed = APPROVAL_DOC in changed_set

    if not adr_changed:
        failures.append(
            "safety-path change requires an ADR changed in this same diff; none present"
        )
        checks_ok = False
    if not approval_changed:
        failures.append(
            f"safety-path change requires {APPROVAL_DOC} changed in this same diff"
        )
        checks_ok = False

    if adr_changed:
        adr_text = ""
        for p in adr_changed:
            adr_text += (root / p).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") + "\n"
        for path in safety_changed:
            name = Path(path).name
            module = Path(path).stem
            if name not in adr_text and module not in adr_text:
                failures.append(
                    f"changed safety path {path} is not referenced by any ADR "
                    "changed in this same diff"
                )
                checks_ok = False

    approval_path = root / APPROVAL_DOC
    if approval_path.exists():
        txt = approval_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
        if "APPROVED" not in txt or "leo" not in txt:
            failures.append(
                f"{APPROVAL_DOC} must carry the real APPROVED marker and owner 'leo'"
            )
            checks_ok = False
    if checks_ok:
        print("safety-path change carries a changed ADR + updated approval evidence")

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Gate 2: static/type/dependency + boundary.")
    add_change_args(parser)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    root: Path = resolve_root(args.root)
    checks: list[str] = []
    failures: list[str] = []

    ruff = tool_path(root, "ruff")
    proc = run([ruff, "check", "."], root)
    checks.append(f"ruff check . -> exit {proc.returncode}")
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        findings = [
            line for line in (proc.stdout or "").splitlines()
            if ": error:" in line or ": warning:" in line
        ]
        if not findings:
            findings = (proc.stdout or "").splitlines()[:40]
        failures.append("ruff reported lint findings:")
        failures.extend(f"  {f}" for f in findings)

    mypy = tool_path(root, "mypy")
    mproc = run(

        root,
    )
    checks.append(f"mypy src/research_desk -> exit {mproc.returncode}")
    if mproc.returncode != 0:
        findings = [
            line for line in (mproc.stdout or "").splitlines() if ": error:" in line
        ]
        if not findings:
            findings = (mproc.stdout or "").splitlines()[:40]
        failures.append("mypy reported type findings (src/research_desk):")
        failures.extend(f"  {f}" for f in findings)

    py = tool_path(root, "python") or "python"
    pproc = run([py, "-m", "pip", "check"], root)
    checks.append(f"pip check -> exit {pproc.returncode}")
    if pproc.returncode != 0:

    except RuntimeError as exc:
        fail(checks, [f"could not resolve changed files: {exc}"])
    if changed:
        check_safety_path_evidence(root, changed, failures)

    fail(checks, failures)

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import jsonschema
import yaml

from _gate_lib import add_change_args, fail, resolve_root

FIT_OPERATORS = {"==", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="}
AT_RE = re.compile(r"^AT-(\d{2})$")
TRACE_MATRIX_CANDIDATES = (
    "docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md",
    "docs/architecture/trace-matrix.yaml",
    "docs/architecture/trace-matrix.yml",

)


def _at_test_targets(root: Path, at_id: str) -> list[Path] | None:
    """Return the files that must exist for an AT id, or None if malformed."""
    m = AT_RE.match(at_id)
    if not m:
        return None
    n = int(m.group(1))
    if 1 <= n <= 6:
        return sorted((root / "test/offline").glob(f"test_at{n:02d}_*.py"))
    if n == 7:
        return [root / "src/research_desk/eval"]
    if n == 8:
        return sorted((root / "scripts").glob("check_*.py"))
    return None


def _resolve_component(root: Path, comp: str) -> tuple[Path, bool]:
    if comp.startswith("research_desk."):
        p = root / "src" / (comp.replace(".", "/") + ".py")
        return p, p.exists()
    if comp.startswith("tradingagents."):
        p = root / comp.replace(".", "/")
        return p, (p.with_suffix(".py").exists() or p.is_dir())
    if comp == "scripts":
        p = root / "scripts"
        return p, p.is_dir()
    if comp.startswith(".github/"):
        p = root / comp
        return p, p.exists()
    p = root / comp
    return p, p.exists()


def _is_url(value: str) -> bool:
    return value.startswith("http://") or value.startswith("https://")


def _matrix_rows(matrix_text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map requirement id -> concatenated row text (all cells after the id)."""
    rows: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in matrix_text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line.startswith("|"):
            continue
        cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip("|").split("|")]
        if not cells:
            continue
        rid = cells[0]
        if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]+-\d{3}", rid):
            rows[rid] = " ".join(cells[1:])
    return rows

    failures: list[str] = []

    schema_path = root / "docs/req/req-schema.json"

    if not reg_path.exists():

    schema = json.loads(schema_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    registry = yaml.safe_load(reg_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    checks.append(f"read {reg_path}")

    if not isinstance(registry, dict):
        fail(checks, ["requirements.yaml is not a YAML mapping"])
    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
        fail(checks, ["req-schema.json is not a JSON object"])

    if "schema_version" not in registry:
        failures.append("registry missing top-level schema_version")
    if "product" not in registry:
        failures.append("registry missing top-level product")
    reqs = registry.get("requirements")
    if not isinstance(reqs, list) or not reqs:
        failures.append("registry requirements must be a non-empty list")
        reqs = []

    try:
        jsonschema.validate(instance=registry, schema=schema)
        checks.append("registry validates against req-schema.json")
    except jsonschema.ValidationError as exc:
        failures.append(f"registry does not match req-schema.json: {exc.message}")

    ids: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for i, req in enumerate(reqs):
        if not isinstance(req, dict):
            failures.append(f"requirements[{i}] is not a mapping")
            continue
        rid = req.get("id")
        if not isinstance(rid, str):
            failures.append(f"requirements[{i}] missing id")
            continue
        ids.append(rid)
        if rid in seen:

        fit = req.get("fit") or {}
        if not isinstance(fit, dict):

        else:
            metric = fit.get("metric")
            operator = fit.get("operator")
            threshold = fit.get("threshold")
            verification = fit.get("verification")
            if not metric:
                failures.append(f"{rid}: fit.metric is empty")
            if operator not in FIT_OPERATORS:
                failures.append(f"{rid}: fit.operator {operator!r} not in {sorted(FIT_OPERATORS)}")
            try:
                float(str(threshold))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                failures.append(f"{rid}: fit.threshold {threshold!r} is not numeric")
            if not verification:
                failures.append(f"{rid}: fit.verification is empty")

        for source in req.get("source") or []:
            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:

                continue
            if _is_url(source):

                continue
            sp = root / source
            if not sp.exists():

        for comp in req.get("components") or []:
            _, ok = _resolve_component(root, comp)
            if not ok:
                failures.append(f"{rid}: component link broken -> {comp}")

        for tid in req.get("tests") or []:

                if not (root / "tests").is_dir():
                    failures.append(f"{rid}: upstream-regression target tests/ missing")
                continue
            targets = _at_test_targets(root, tid)
            if targets is None:
                failures.append(f"{rid}: malformed test id {tid!r}")
                continue
            if not targets or not any(t.exists() for t in targets):
                failures.append(f"{rid}: test link broken -> {tid} ({targets})")

    matrix_path = None
    for cand in TRACE_MATRIX_CANDIDATES:
        if (root / cand).exists():
            matrix_path = root / cand
            break
    if matrix_path is None:
        failures.append(
            "trace matrix not found (expected docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md); "
            "cannot verify full requirement->test traceability"
        )
    else:
        matrix_text = matrix_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        rows = _matrix_rows(matrix_text)
        checks.append(f"trace matrix rows: {len(rows)}")
        matrix_ids = set(rows.keys())
        missing_from_matrix = sorted(set(ids) - matrix_ids)
        if missing_from_matrix:
            failures.append(f"requirement IDs absent from trace matrix: {missing_from_matrix}")
        extra_in_matrix = sorted(matrix_ids - set(ids))
        if extra_in_matrix:
            failures.append(f"trace matrix lists unknown requirement IDs: {extra_in_matrix}")
        for req in reqs:

            if not row_text:

                        f"{rid}: test {tid} is missing from this requirement's own "
                        "trace-matrix row"
                    )

    checks.append(f"requirement count: {len(reqs)}")
    fail(checks, failures)

class _NetworkBlock:
    """Blocks real socket I/O and counts any attempted external call."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.attempts = 0

    def _block(self, *args, **kwargs):  # noqa: ANN002,ANN003
        self.attempts += 1
        raise OSError("network blocked during offline gate")


def _grounded_message(case: dict) -> str:
    """A grounded prompt carrying each case's real identity/date/price/source facts."""
    lines = [
        "STANDING ANALYSIS CONSTRAINTS (always true for this run):",
        f"Instrument identity: {case['ticker']}",
        f"Company: {case['identity']['company_name']}",
        f"Sector/industry: {case['identity']['sector']} / {case['identity']['industry']}",
        f"Analysis date: {case['analysis_date']}",
        f"Announcement date: {case['announcement_date']}",
        f"last_close: {case['latest_close']}",
        f"source_id: {case['source_id']}",
        f"source_url: {case['source_url']}",
        "Evidence notes:",
    ]
    lines += [f"- {note}" for note in case["notes"]]
    lines.append("Balance guidance: " + case["balance"])
    # Verbose padding prose so trimming would apply were the fact markers absent.
    for i in range(8):
        lines.append(f"verbose analyst draft paragraph {i}: " + "non-grounding filler text. " * 30)
    return "\n".join(lines)

            out_text = "\n".join(

            facts = [

                case["source_url"],

            for fact in facts:

                "fixed captured-output + prompt-transform gate applies (live quality "
                "requires the recorded release experiment)"
            )

    fail(checks, failures)

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

from _gate_lib import add_change_args, changed_files, fail, resolve_root

LOG_PATH = "docs/ai-use-log.yaml"
REQUIRED_ENTRY_FIELDS = ("date", "tool", "model", "purpose", "session", "prompt", "scope", "review", "outcome")


def is_code_or_prompt_change(path: str) -> bool:
    lower = path.lower()
    if path.endswith(".py"):
        return True
    if "prompt" in lower:
        return True
    if "/prompts/" in lower:
        return True
    return False


def covers(scope_item: str, file_path: str) -> bool:
    scope_item = scope_item.rstrip("/")
    if not scope_item:
        return False
    if file_path == scope_item:
        return True
    return file_path.startswith(scope_item + "/")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Gate 6: AI-use log required for code/prompt changes.")
    add_change_args(parser)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    root: Path = resolve_root(args.root)
    checks: list[str] = []
    failures: list[str] = []

    try:
        changed = changed_files(root, args.base_ref, args.head_ref, args.changed_files)
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        fail(checks, [f"could not resolve changed files: {exc}"])

    code_prompt = sorted(c for c in changed if is_code_or_prompt_change(c))
    checks.append(f"changed files: {len(changed)}")
    checks.append(f"code/prompt changes requiring a log update: {len(code_prompt)}")

    if not code_prompt:
        checks.append("no code/prompt changes; AI-use log not required for this change set")
        fail(checks, failures)

    log_file = root / LOG_PATH
    if not log_file.exists():
        fail(checks, [f"code/prompt changed but {LOG_PATH} is missing"])

    try:
        data = yaml.safe_load(log_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
        fail(checks, [f"{LOG_PATH} is not valid YAML: {exc}"])

    checks.append(f"read {LOG_PATH}")

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        fail(checks, [f"{LOG_PATH} is not a YAML mapping"])

    for key in ("schema_version", "project", "decision_owner"):
        if not data.get(key):
            failures.append(f"{LOG_PATH} missing top-level key: {key}")

    entries = data.get("entries")
    if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
        failures.append(f"{LOG_PATH} must have a non-empty entries list")

    covered: set[str] = set()
    valid_entries = 0
    for i, entry in enumerate(entries or []):
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            failures.append(f"entries[{i}] is not a mapping")
            continue
        valid_entries += 1
        for field in REQUIRED_ENTRY_FIELDS:
            if field not in entry or entry[field] in (None, ""):
                failures.append(f"entries[{i}] missing required field: {field}")
        scope = entry.get("scope")
        if scope is not None and not isinstance(scope, list):
            failures.append(f"entries[{i}] scope must be a list")
            scope = []
        for file_path in code_prompt:
            if any(covers(str(s), file_path) for s in (scope or [])):
                covered.add(file_path)

    checks.append(f"log entries: {len(entries or [])} (valid: {valid_entries})")

    uncovered = [f for f in code_prompt if f not in covered]
    if uncovered:
        failures.append("changed code/prompt files not covered by any log entry scope:")
        failures.extend(f"  {f}" for f in uncovered)
    else:
        checks.append("all changed code/prompt files are covered by a log entry scope")

    fail(checks, failures)

-## TradingAgents Framework
-
-TradingAgents is a multi-agent trading framework that mirrors the dynamics of real-world trading firms. By deploying specialized LLM-powered agents: from fundamental analysts, sentiment experts, and technical analysts, to trader, risk management team, the platform collaboratively evaluates market conditions and informs trading decisions. Moreover, these agents engage in dynamic discussions to pinpoint the optimal strategy.
-
-<p align="center">
-  <img src="assets/schema.png" style="width: 100%; height: auto;">
-</p>
-
-> TradingAgents framework is designed for research purposes. Trading performance may vary based on many factors, including the chosen backbone language models, model temperature, trading periods, the quality of data, and other non-deterministic factors. [It is not intended as financial, investment, or trading advice.](https://tauric.ai/disclaimer/)
-
-Our framework decomposes complex trading tasks into specialized roles.
-
-### Analyst Team
-- Fundamentals Analyst: Evaluates company financials and performance metrics, identifying intrinsic values and potential red flags.
-- Sentiment Analyst: Aggregates news headlines, StockTwits, and Reddit chatter into a single sentiment read to gauge short-term market mood.
-- News Analyst: Monitors global news and macroeconomic indicators, interpreting the impact of events on market conditions.
-- Technical Analyst: Utilizes technical indicators (like MACD and RSI) to detect trading patterns and forecast price movements.
-

-</p>
-
-### Researcher Team
-- Comprises both bullish and bearish researchers who critically assess the insights provided by the Analyst Team. Through structured debates, they balance potential gains against inherent risks.
-

-</p>
-
-### Trader Agent
-- Composes reports from the analysts and researchers to make informed trading decisions, determining the timing and magnitude of trades.

-
-### Risk Management and Portfolio Manager
-- Continuously evaluates portfolio risk by assessing market volatility, liquidity, and other risk factors. The risk management team evaluates and adjusts trading strategies, providing assessment reports to the Portfolio Manager for final decision.
-- The Portfolio Manager approves/rejects the transaction proposal. If approved, the order will be sent to the simulated exchange and executed.

-## Persistence and Recovery
-
-TradingAgents persists two kinds of state across runs.
-
-### Decision log
-
-The decision log is always on. Each completed run appends its decision to `~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md`. On the next run for the same ticker, TradingAgents fetches the realised return (raw and alpha vs SPY), generates a one-paragraph reflection, and injects the most recent same-ticker decisions plus recent cross-ticker lessons into the Portfolio Manager prompt, so each analysis carries forward what worked and what didn't.
-
-Override the path with `TRADINGAGENTS_MEMORY_LOG_PATH`.
-
-### Checkpoint resume
-
-Checkpoint resume is opt-in via `--checkpoint`. When enabled, LangGraph saves state after each node so a crashed or interrupted run resumes from the last successful step instead of starting over. On a resume run you will see `Resuming from step N for <TICKER> on <date>` in the logs; on a new run you will see `Starting fresh`. Checkpoints are cleared automatically on successful completion.
-
-Per-ticker SQLite databases live at `~/.tradingagents/cache/checkpoints/<TICKER>.db` (override the base with `TRADINGAGENTS_CACHE_DIR`). Use `--clear-checkpoints` to reset all of them before a run.
-
-```bash
-tradingagents analyze --checkpoint           # enable for this run
-tradingagents analyze --clear-checkpoints    # reset before running
-```
-
-```python
-config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()
-config["checkpoint_enabled"] = True
-ta = TradingAgentsGraph(config=config)
-_, decision = ta.propagate("NVDA", "2026-01-15")
-```
-
-## Reproducibility
-
-TradingAgents is LLM-driven, so two runs of the same ticker and date can differ. This is expected for a research tool built on language models, not a defect. The variation comes from a few distinct sources, and it helps to separate them.
-
-Language model sampling is non-deterministic. Even at a fixed temperature, providers do not guarantee byte-identical output across calls, and reasoning models (the default GPT-5.x family, and any thinking-mode model) vary the most because their internal reasoning is itself sampled.
-
-Live data moves. News, StockTwits, and Reddit return different content as time passes, so a run today sees different inputs than a run last week even for the same historical trade date. Pin the analysis date to hold the price and indicator window fixed, but the social and news sources still reflect "now".
-
-To reduce variation you can lower the sampling temperature. Set `temperature` in your config (or `TRADINGAGENTS_TEMPERATURE` in `.env`); lower values make models that honor it more repeatable. The current curated models are reasoning-first and largely ignore temperature, so for tighter reproducibility use a non-reasoning model, which you can set explicitly via the Custom model ID option.
-
-```python
-config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()

+## TradingAgents Framework
+
+TradingAgents is a multi-agent trading framework that mirrors the dynamics of real-world trading firms. By deploying specialized LLM-powered agents: from fundamental analysts, sentiment experts, and technical analysts, to trader, risk management team, the platform collaboratively evaluates market conditions and informs trading decisions. Moreover, these agents engage in dynamic discussions to pinpoint the optimal strategy.
+
+<p align="center">
+  <img src="assets/schema.png" style="width: 100%; height: auto;">
+</p>
+
+> TradingAgents framework is designed for research purposes. Trading performance may vary based on many factors, including the chosen backbone language models, model temperature, trading periods, the quality of data, and other non-deterministic factors. [It is not intended as financial, investment, or trading advice.](https://tauric.ai/disclaimer/)
+
+Our framework decomposes complex trading tasks into specialized roles.
+
+### Analyst Team
+- Fundamentals Analyst: Evaluates company financials and performance metrics, identifying intrinsic values and potential red flags.
+- Sentiment Analyst: Aggregates news headlines, StockTwits, and Reddit chatter into a single sentiment read to gauge short-term market mood.
+- News Analyst: Monitors global news and macroeconomic indicators, interpreting the impact of events on market conditions.
+- Technical Analyst: Utilizes technical indicators (like MACD and RSI) to detect trading patterns and forecast price movements.
+
+<p align="center">
+  <img src="assets/analyst.png" width="100%" style="display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;">
+</p>
+
+### Researcher Team
+- Comprises both bullish and bearish researchers who critically assess the insights provided by the Analyst Team. Through structured debates, they balance potential gains against inherent risks.
+
+<p align="center">
+  <img src="assets/researcher.png" width="70%" style="display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;">
+</p>
+
+### Trader Agent
+- Composes reports from the analysts and researchers to make informed trading decisions, determining the timing and magnitude of trades.
+
+<p align="center">
+  <img src="assets/trader.png" width="70%" style="display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;">
+</p>
+
+### Risk Management and Portfolio Manager
+- Continuously evaluates portfolio risk by assessing market volatility, liquidity, and other risk factors. The risk management team evaluates and adjusts trading strategies, providing assessment reports to the Portfolio Manager for final decision.
+- The Portfolio Manager approves/rejects the transaction proposal. If approved, the order will be sent to the simulated exchange and executed.

+## Installation and CLI
+
+### Installation
+
+Clone TradingAgents:
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents.git
+cd TradingAgents
+```
+
+Create a virtual environment in any of your favorite environment managers:
+```bash
+conda create -n tradingagents python=3.12
+conda activate tradingagents
+```
+
+Install the package and its dependencies:
+```bash
+pip install .
+```
+
+### Docker
+
+Alternatively, run with Docker:
+```bash
+cp .env.example .env  # add your API keys
+docker compose run --rm tradingagents
+```
+
+For local models with Ollama:
+```bash
+docker compose --profile ollama run --rm tradingagents-ollama
+```
+
+### Required APIs
+
+TradingAgents supports multiple LLM providers. Set the API key for your chosen provider:
+
+```bash
+export OPENAI_API_KEY=...          # OpenAI (GPT)
+export GOOGLE_API_KEY=...          # Google (Gemini)
+export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...       # Anthropic (Claude)
+export XAI_API_KEY=...             # xAI (Grok)
+export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=...        # DeepSeek
+export DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=...       # Qwen — International (dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com)
+export DASHSCOPE_CN_API_KEY=...    # Qwen — China (dashscope.aliyuncs.com)
+export ZHIPU_API_KEY=...           # GLM via Z.AI (international)
+export ZHIPU_CN_API_KEY=...        # GLM via BigModel (China, open.bigmodel.cn)
+export MINIMAX_API_KEY=...         # MiniMax — Global (api.minimax.io)
+export MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY=...      # MiniMax — China (api.minimaxi.com)
+export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...      # OpenRouter
+export ALPHA_VANTAGE_API_KEY=...   # Alpha Vantage
+```
+
+For Azure OpenAI, copy `.env.enterprise.example` to `.env.enterprise` and fill in your credentials.
+
+For AWS Bedrock, install the extra with `pip install ".[bedrock]"`, set `llm_provider: "bedrock"`, configure AWS credentials (environment variables, `~/.aws/credentials`, or an IAM role) and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, and use a Bedrock model ID, e.g. `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`.
+
+For local models, configure Ollama with `llm_provider: "ollama"`. The default endpoint is `http://localhost:11434/v1`; set `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` to point at a remote `ollama-serve`. Pull models with `ollama pull <name>`, and pick "Custom model ID" in the CLI for any model not listed by default.
+
+For any other OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or a custom relay), use `llm_provider: "openai_compatible"` and set the endpoint via `backend_url` (or `TRADINGAGENTS_LLM_BACKEND_URL`), e.g. `http://localhost:8000/v1` for vLLM or `http://localhost:1234/v1` for LM Studio. The model is whatever your server serves. No key is needed for local servers; set `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY` when the endpoint requires one.
+
+Alternatively, copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in your keys:
+```bash
+cp .env.example .env
+```

+### CLI Usage

+Launch the interactive CLI:
+```bash
+tradingagents          # installed command
+python -m cli.main     # alternative: run directly from source

+## TradingAgents Package
+
+### Implementation Details
+
+We built TradingAgents with LangGraph to ensure flexibility and modularity. The framework supports multiple LLM providers: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek, Qwen (Alibaba DashScope, international and China endpoints), GLM (Zhipu), MiniMax (global + China), OpenRouter, Ollama for local models, and Azure OpenAI for enterprise.
+
+### Python Usage
+
+To use TradingAgents inside your code, you can import the `tradingagents` module and initialize a `TradingAgentsGraph()` object. The `.propagate()` function will return a decision. You can run `main.py`, here's also a quick example:
+
+```python
+from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph
+from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG
+
+ta = TradingAgentsGraph(debug=True, config=DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy())
+
+# forward propagate
+_, decision = ta.propagate("NVDA", "2026-01-15")
+print(decision)
+```
+
+You can also adjust the default configuration to set your own choice of LLMs, debate rounds, etc.
+
+```python
+from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph
+from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG
+
+config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()
+config["llm_provider"] = "openai"        # e.g. openai, google, anthropic, deepseek, groq, ollama; openai_compatible covers any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, ...)
+config["deep_think_llm"] = "gpt-5.6"      # Model for complex reasoning
+config["quick_think_llm"] = "gpt-5.6-luna" # Model for quick tasks
+config["max_debate_rounds"] = 2
+
+ta = TradingAgentsGraph(debug=True, config=config)
+_, decision = ta.propagate("NVDA", "2026-01-15")
+print(decision)
+```
+
+See `tradingagents/default_config.py` for all configuration options.
+
+## Persistence and Recovery
+
+TradingAgents persists two kinds of state across runs.
+
+### Decision log
+
+The decision log is always on. Each completed run appends its decision to `~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md`. On the next run for the same ticker, TradingAgents fetches the realised return (raw and alpha vs SPY), generates a one-paragraph reflection, and injects the most recent same-ticker decisions plus recent cross-ticker lessons into the Portfolio Manager prompt, so each analysis carries forward what worked and what didn't.
+
+Override the path with `TRADINGAGENTS_MEMORY_LOG_PATH`.
+
+### Checkpoint resume
+
+Checkpoint resume is opt-in via `--checkpoint`. When enabled, LangGraph saves state after each node so a crashed or interrupted run resumes from the last successful step instead of starting over. On a resume run you will see `Resuming from step N for <TICKER> on <date>` in the logs; on a new run you will see `Starting fresh`. Checkpoints are cleared automatically on successful completion.
+
+Per-ticker SQLite databases live at `~/.tradingagents/cache/checkpoints/<TICKER>.db` (override the base with `TRADINGAGENTS_CACHE_DIR`). Use `--clear-checkpoints` to reset all of them before a run.
+
+```bash
+tradingagents analyze --checkpoint           # enable for this run
+tradingagents analyze --clear-checkpoints    # reset before running
+```
+
+```python
+config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()
+config["checkpoint_enabled"] = True
+ta = TradingAgentsGraph(config=config)
+_, decision = ta.propagate("NVDA", "2026-01-15")
+```
+
+## Reproducibility
+
+TradingAgents is LLM-driven, so two runs of the same ticker and date can differ. This is expected for a research tool built on language models, not a defect. The variation comes from a few distinct sources, and it helps to separate them.
+
+Language model sampling is non-deterministic. Even at a fixed temperature, providers do not guarantee byte-identical output across calls, and reasoning models (the default GPT-5.x family, and any thinking-mode model) vary the most because their internal reasoning is itself sampled.
+
+Live data moves. News, StockTwits, and Reddit return different content as time passes, so a run today sees different inputs than a run last week even for the same historical trade date. Pin the analysis date to hold the price and indicator window fixed, but the social and news sources still reflect "now".
+
+To reduce variation you can lower the sampling temperature. Set `temperature` in your config (or `TRADINGAGENTS_TEMPERATURE` in `.env`); lower values make models that honor it more repeatable. The current curated models are reasoning-first and largely ignore temperature, so for tighter reproducibility use a non-reasoning model, which you can set explicitly via the Custom model ID option.
+
+```python
+config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()
+config["llm_provider"] = "openai"
+config["temperature"] = 0.0
+# Reasoning models ignore temperature. For tighter reproducibility, set a
+# non-reasoning deep/quick model explicitly (e.g. via the Custom model ID option).
+```
+
+What does not vary anymore: the analyzed company identity is resolved deterministically from the ticker before any agent runs, and the market analyst grounds exact price and indicator claims in a verified data snapshot. Earlier reports of "different companies" or fabricated price levels across runs are addressed by these two mechanisms.
+
+Backtest results are not guaranteed to match any published figure. Returns depend on the model, the temperature, the date range, data quality, and the sampling above. Treat the framework as a research scaffold for studying multi-agent analysis, not as a strategy with a fixed, replicable return.

 def _judge_prompt(case: dict, report_text: str, deterministic: list[dict]) -> str:
     notes = "\n".join(f"- {n}" for n in case.get("notes", []))
     facts = "\n".join(
         f"- {c['check']}: {'PASS' if c['passed'] else 'FAIL'} ({c['detail']})"
         for c in deterministic
     )
     return f"""You are an independent equity-research evaluator (a separate role from the analyst).
 
 Evidence (frozen official source, source_id {case.get('source_id', 'n/a')}):
 {notes}
 
 Frozen latest close: {case['latest_close']:.2f}
 
 Deterministic checks already computed against the report:
 {facts}
 
 Judge the report below. Score support and relevance on 0-1 using the rubric:
 - support 1.0 = every key conclusion has direct support from the evidence; 0.8 = main conclusions supported with no key fabrication; 0.5 = important evidence gaps; 0 = key factual fabrication.
 - relevance 1.0 = fully focused on the requested ticker/date/task; 0.8 = core complete with minor redundancy; 0.5 = missing key parts; 0 = off task.
 Do NOT give 1.0 just because the report is nonempty. List which source IDs are valid citations (present and actually supporting the cited claim) and which factual claims are uncited.
 
 REPORT:
 {report_text}
 """
 
 
 def _llm_judge(case: dict, report_text: str, deterministic: list[dict]):
     """Run the real DeepSeek evaluator; returns (raw, score) without fabrication."""
     from langchain_core.utils.function_calling import convert_to_openai_tool
     from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
 
     from tradingagents.llm_clients import create_llm_client
 
     class _Judge(BaseModel):
         support: float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
         relevance: float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
         valid_citation_ids: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
         uncited_factual_claims: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
         rationale: str = ""
 
     client = create_llm_client(
         PROVIDER,
         MODEL,
         base_url=os.environ.get("DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL"),
         max_tokens=OUTPUT_CAP,
         temperature=0,
     )
     llm = client.get_llm()
     if hasattr(llm, "extra_body"):
         llm.extra_body = dict(THINKING_DISABLED_EXTRA_BODY)
 
     prompt = _judge_prompt(case, report_text, deterministic)
     structured = llm.with_structured_output(_Judge, include_raw=True)
     raw_out = structured.invoke(prompt)
 
     raw_resp = raw_out.get("raw", None)
     parsed = raw_out.get("parsed", None)
     usage: dict[str, Any] = {}
     if hasattr(raw_resp, "usage_metadata"):
         usage = dict(raw_resp.usage_metadata or {})
 
     if parsed is None:
         score: dict[str, Any] = {
             "support": None,
             "relevance": None,
             "valid_citation_ids": [],
             "uncited_factual_claims": [],
             "rationale": "judge returned no parseable structured score",
             "error": True,
         }
     else:
         score = {
             "support": float(parsed.support),
             "relevance": float(parsed.relevance),
             "valid_citation_ids": list(parsed.valid_citation_ids),
             "uncited_factual_claims": list(parsed.uncited_factual_claims),
             "rationale": parsed.rationale,
             "error": False,
         }
     raw = {
         "prompt": prompt,
         "response_text": getattr(raw_resp, "content", None) if raw_resp is not None else None,
         "usage": usage,
     }
     return raw, score

 def run_aggregate(root: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Compute six paired baseline/compact metrics from existing run dirs.
 
     No model is called. Completed arms are included; a missing or non-completed
     arm is recorded as such. Judge scores, when present, are attached separately.
     """
     root = Path(root)
     cases = [c for c in (root.iterdir() if root.exists() else []) if c.is_dir()]
     paired: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
     for case_dir in sorted(cases):
         ticker = case_dir.name
         arms = {}
         for mode in ("baseline", "compact"):
             summary = case_dir / mode / "summary.json"
             if not summary.exists():
                 arms[mode] = {"present": False}
                 continue
             data = json.loads(summary.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
             data["present"] = True
             judge_file = root / "judge" / ticker / mode / "judge.json"
             if judge_file.exists():
                 data["judge"] = json.loads(judge_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
             arms[mode] = data
         if not arms.get("baseline", {}).get("present") and not arms.get("compact", {}).get("present"):
             continue
         paired.append({"ticker": ticker, "baseline": arms.get("baseline"), "compact": arms.get("compact")})
     report = _aggregate_report(paired)
     _dump_json(root / "aggregate" / "summary.json", {"paired": paired})
     (root / "aggregate" / "report.md").write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
     return {"paired": paired, "report": report}
 
 
 def _arm_value(arm: dict | None, key: str, default=None):
     if arm is None or not arm.get("present"):
         return default
     return arm.get(key, default)
 
 
 def _aggregate_report(paired: list[dict]) -> str:
     lines = [
         "# Baseline / Compact Aggregate (six paired metrics)",
         "",
         "Read from existing run outputs; no model calls. Judge scores are attached when present.",
         "",
         "| ticker | metric | baseline | compact | delta |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|",
     ]
     metrics = [
         ("calls", "{:.0f}"),
         ("input_tokens", "{:.0f}"),
         ("output_tokens", "{:.0f}"),
         ("total_tokens", "{:.0f}"),
         ("wall_seconds", "{:.1f}"),
         ("outcome", "{!s}"),
     ]
     for p in paired:
         t = p["ticker"]
         for key, fmt in metrics:
             b = _arm_value(p.get("baseline"), key)
             c = _arm_value(p.get("compact"), key)
             b_s = "n/a" if b is None else fmt.format(b)
             c_s = "n/a" if c is None else fmt.format(c)
             delta = "—"
             if isinstance(b, (int, float)) and isinstance(c, (int, float)):
                 delta = _pct(b, c)
             lines.append(f"| {t} | {key} | {b_s} | {c_s} | {delta} |")
     for p in paired:
         for mode in ("baseline", "compact"):
             judge = _arm_value(p.get(mode), "judge")
             if isinstance(judge, dict) and not judge.get("error") and judge.get("support") is not None:
                 lines.append(
                     f"| {p['ticker']} | {mode} judge support | {judge['support']:.2f} | — | — |"
                 )
                 lines.append(
                     f"| {p['ticker']} | {mode} judge relevance | {judge['relevance']:.2f} | — | — |"
                 )
     return "\n".join(lines)
 
 
 def _pct(b: float, c: float) -> str:
     if b == 0:
         return "—"
     return f"{(c - b) / b * 100:+.1f}%"

+              "patch": "Index: docs/architecture/adr/ADR-001-evidence-pack-format.md\n===================================================================\n--- docs/architecture/adr/ADR-001-evidence-pack-format.md\t\n+++ docs/architecture/adr/ADR-001-evidence-pack-format.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@\n+# ADR-001: Evidence pack format and offline replay\n+\n+Status: accepted (2026-08-31, decided by leo). Context: F1.\n+\n+## Decision\n+\n+An evidence pack is a self-contained directory (or a ZIP of one) with a fixed\n+set of JSON/JSONL files: `manifest.json`, `input.json`, `events.jsonl`,\n+`final_state.json`, `usage.json`, `calls.json`, optional `proposal.json`, and\n+`meta.json`. `complete` is only set when every required file is present and\n+parses. Import validates required files and fails loudly on a missing record.\n+\n+Replay rebuilds the report tree from `final_state`, derives the signal with the\n+same deterministic heuristic the graph uses (`SignalProcessor`), and reports\n+the deterministic policy bounds for the proposal against a ledger. Replay never\n+constructs an LLM client.\n+\n+## Why\n+\n+- The final graph state plus the captured tool data are the *material* needed\n+  to rebuild reports and policy outputs with zero external calls; LLM re-output\n+  is not needed and would violate \"no network on replay\".\n+- Complete/incomplete is a structural property (required files) so a partial\n+  pack cannot silently replay a wrong decision.\n+- JSONL events keep the log append-friendly and streamable.\n+\n+## Consequences\n+\n+- Evidence packs can be large (they keep full prompts/responses for provenance).\n+- Replay is deterministic for the signal and policy; the *report timestamps*\n+  are display metadata and intentionally differ from the original run.\n",

see ADR-002).\n+- New application lives in `src/research_desk/`; new tests in `test/offline/`;\n+  fixtures in `test/fixtures/`.\n+- Option B (application-layer narrow seam) was chosen: no rewriting of the\n+  graph, no global monkeypatching, no vendor-routing forks.\n+\n+## Modules\n+\n+| Module | Responsibility | Reuses |\n+|---|---|---|\n+| `research_desk/evidence.py` | callback recorder, evidence packs, sanitisation, pack IO | langchain BaseCallbackHandler, upstream report writer |\n+| `research_desk/graph_adapter.py` | `EvidenceTradingGraph` subclass + streaming `ResearchRunner`; frozen tool nodes; price-from-evidence | `TradingAgentsGraph`, `ToolNode`, `write_report_tree` |\n+| `research_desk/context.py` | baseline/compact assembly: dedup, bounded history, constraint re-injection, as-of filter | `TradingMemoryLog` entry shape |\n+| `research_desk/budget.py` | LLM call budget + provider-usage accounting | upstream `max_tokens` config |\n+| `research_desk/review.py` | proposal state machine + execution; `policy.py` deterministic checks | `rating` vocabulary |\n+| `research_desk/storage.py` | SQLite ledger/proposals/transactions; JSON pack IO | stdlib sqlite3 |\n+| `research_desk/replay.py` | offline replay (zero external calls) | `SignalProcessor`, `write_report_tree` |\n+| `research_desk/cli.py` | analyze/export/replay/propose/review/execute/ledger/compare | typer/rich |\n+\n+## Flow\n+\n+```mermaid\n+flowchart LR\n+    U[operator] --> C[CLI]\n+    C --> R[ResearchRunner]\n+    R --> X[ContextAssembler baseline/compact]\n+    X --> T[TradingAgentsGraph + EvidenceTradingGraph]\n+    T --> E[EvidenceRecorder + BudgetTracker]\n+    T --> P[final state / signal]\n+    E --> P\n+    P --> EP[Evidence pack]\n+    EP --> RV[Replay - zero external calls]\n+    P --> PR[PENDING_REVIEW proposal]\n+    U --> A[approve/reject - operator only]\n+    A --> PR\n+    PR --> G[deterministic policy]\n+    G --> L[SQLite ledger - idempotent SIMULATED]\n+```\n+\n+## Data\n+\n+- Evidence pack: `manifest.json`, `input.json`, `events.jsonl`, `final_state.json`,\n+  `usage.json`, `calls.json`, optional `proposal.json`, `meta.json`.\n+- Ledger: SQLite `ledger_state` (single row), `positions`, `proposals`,\n+  `transactions`. WAL journal; single writer; atomic per-transaction commits.\n+\n+## Scope decisions (offline slice)\n+\n+- Analysts: `market`, `news`; US equities; sequential runs.\n+- v1 execution is buy-only (no shorting, no sell of holdings).\n+- Replay rebuilds reports + signal + policy bounds deterministically; it never\n+  starts an LLM request. A controlled rerun (`data_mode=frozen`) is the real\n+  graph over frozen evidence and is a separate path.\n+- Live metrics (QUALITY/COST/PERF, six gates on GitHub) are pending; the local\n+  mechanisms exist and are tested offline.\n",

Enforcement happens in the evidence recorder's\n+``on_chat_model_start``: once the configured call limit is reached, the next\n+call raises :class:`BudgetExhausted` so the graph aborts and no further LLM\n+request is started (NFR-003).
